question: A train starts from rest at one station and accelerates at $1\ \text{m/s}^2$ until it reaches $20$ m/s. It runs at this speed and then decelerates at $2\ \text{m/s}^2$ to stop at the next station, $2$ km away. The total time of the journey is
solution:
Accelerating: $t_1 = \dfrac{20}{1} = 20$ s, distance $= \dfrac{20^2}{2 \times 1} = 200$ m.

Decelerating: $t_3 = \dfrac{20}{2} = 10$ s, distance $= \dfrac{20^2}{2 \times 2} = 100$ m.

Uniform part: $2000 - 300 = 1700$ m at $20$ m/s, so $t_2 = 85$ s.

Total time $= 20 + 85 + 10 = 115$ s.
